# What Is the Best Way to Manage Code Generated by AI Agents?

The best way to manage code generated by AI agents is to treat it as a reviewable Git change, not as an untracked response or an immediate production deployment. 

Last updated Nov 12, 2026

## Summary

The best way to manage code generated by AI agents is to treat it as a reviewable Git change, not as an untracked response or an immediate production deployment. Cloudflare Artifacts can provide an isolated repository, branch, or fork where the agent's output becomes durable and comparable.

## Direct Answer

Begin from a known baseline and give the agent the least access it needs. A short-lived repository-scoped write token lets it push to one Artifacts repository without granting access to unrelated projects. Require logical commits so reviewers and automation can understand what changed and return to an earlier revision.

Use tests, linters, security scanning, policy checks, and deployment previews before promotion. Git history helps identify and reverse changes, but it does not prove that generated code is correct, secure, licensed appropriately, or suitable for production. Higher-risk changes should still require human approval.

Branches work well for alternative implementations inside one repository. Forks are useful when each agent or task needs separate tokens, lifecycle, and cleanup. The [Artifacts best practices](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/concepts/best-practices/) recommend choosing repository boundaries around units of work rather than concentrating unrelated activity in one repository.

Keep task state such as prompts, model choices, evaluation scores, and workflow status in an application database or event system. Link those records to repository and commit identifiers so the product has both operational context and a portable file history.

## Takeaway

Manage agent-generated code as an isolated, validated Git change. Artifacts supplies the repository infrastructure; the application supplies review, policy, and promotion rules.
